correctness.rationale: The objects are total maps on X, restricted only by f(Y) being contained in Z. Once a path enters Y it enters Z and never leaves, so cycles are wholly in Z or wholly outside Y. For specified cyclic vertices and permutations, delete their outgoing cycle edges. The noncyclic vertices in Z form a forest rooted at the a cyclic Z vertices and vertices in Y outside Z have k independent target choices each. Outside Y the forest roots are the m vertices of Y together with the b designated cyclic vertices outside Y, since no path can return to the exterior after entering Y. The rooted complete-graph forest minor is NI-J on the nonroots, giving r N^(N-r-1), with the empty minor equal to 1. These choices are independent and recover the map uniquely. Choosing the root sets and the two permutations yields (1); partition summation yields (2). Normalizing the product gives independence and the two probabilities, including the all-root case w=0. The stable image supports a permutation, so eventual period is the lcm, with divisor Möbius inversion valid. Bidegrees recover k and w; for fixed k,w the coefficient sum k^m(m+w)^w is strictly increasing in m except for the stated singleton family.
residual_risks: The replay compares all cycle-type pairs for 35 nested-set cardinality triples n<=5, covering 9055 maps and reproducing the displayed (5,3,2) example. The frozen checker is additional recorded finite evidence; the proof establishes the unrestricted parameter range.
